nodes.summary: The decay length is positive for positive `D` and `k`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the decay length

nodes.summary: The decay length `λ = √(D / k)` of a morphogen with diffusion coefficient `D` and linear degradation rate `k` (both positive in the model).
nodes.title: Decay length of a morphogen gradient
Diffusion coefficient over squared decay length equals degradation rate

nodes.summary: Every bounded steady state with source flux `j` is the exponential profile on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness

nodes.summary: The exponential profile is a bounded steady state with source flux `j`.
nodes.title: Exponential profile is a bounded steady state

nodes.summary: A bounded steady state of the synthesis–diffusion–degradation model on `[0, ∞)`, with `c' = dc/dx`: `D c'' = k c` for `x > 0`, `c` and `c'` continuous up to the source, source flux `-D c'(0) = j`, and `c` bounded on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Bounded steady state of the synthesis–diffusion–degradation model

nodes.summary: A cell at `x` is at or above threshold `θ` iff it lies within the boundary `x_θ`: `θ ≤ c(x) ↔ x ≤ x_θ`.
nodes.title: French-flag regions

nodes.summary: For positive parameters and threshold `θ`, `c(x) = θ` exactly at `x = x_θ = λ log(c(0)/θ)`.
nodes.title: French-flag boundary

nodes.summary: The profile is strictly decreasing in `x` for a positive source.
nodes.title: Morphogen profile is strictly decreasing

nodes.summary: The profile equals `θ` at the boundary `x_θ`.
nodes.title: Profile equals the threshold at the French-flag boundary

nodes.summary: The steady-state gradient `c(x) = (j / √(D k)) e^{-x/λ}`, `λ = √(D / k)`, for source flux `j` at `x = 0`. Meaningful for `D, k > 0`.
nodes.title: Steady-state exponential morphogen profile

nodes.summary: `√(D k) = D / λ`, so the source amplitude is `c(0) = j λ / D`.
nodes.title: Source amplitude in terms of the decay length

nodes.summary: Scaling the source flux by `a > 0` moves every French-flag boundary by `λ log a`.
nodes.title: Boundary shift

nodes.summary: Doubling the source flux shifts every French-flag boundary away from the source by exactly `λ log 2`.
nodes.title: Doubling the source flux shifts boundaries by $\lambda \log 2$

nodes.summary: The French-flag boundary for threshold `θ`: `x_θ = λ log(c(0) / θ)`, where `c(0) = j / √(D k)`. Meaningful for `D, k, j, θ > 0`; it is negative when `θ > c(0)` (no cell is above threshold).
nodes.title: French-flag boundary position for a threshold
